products.title: Rwanda Gitwe Panda Lot 1159
products.body_html:
Origin: Rwanda (Western Province, Nyamasheke)

Washing Station: Gitwe

Lot: 1159

Variety: Red Bourbon

Process: Natural (sun-dried whole cherry)

Elevation: ~1,700–2,000 masl

☕ Roaster’s Note

Rwanda Gitwe Panda – Lot 1159 (Natural Red Bourbon)

This lot expresses a softer, more refined side of Rwanda naturals. Instead of bold, fermented fruit, the cup leans toward delicate tropical brightness and tea-like elegance.

Expect a gentle citrus character reminiscent of pomelo, layered with the subtle sweetness of rambutan and hints of ripe peach. As the cup cools, light berry tones emerge alongside a soft floral lift. The overall profile finishes clean, with a melon tea-like quality that adds to its clarity and drinkability.

The natural process here enhances sweetness without overwhelming the structure, resulting in a cup that is balanced, nuanced, and quietly complex rather than intensely fruit-forward.

🌿 About the Bean

Gitwe sits in Nyamasheke, a region known for its high elevation and proximity to Lake Kivu, which creates a cool microclimate ideal for slow cherry maturation.

Lot 1159 is produced from Red Bourbon trees, a variety that thrives in Rwanda’s volcanic soils. The natural process here means cherries are dried intact on raised beds, allowing sugars and fruit compounds to fully develop before milling.

Rwanda isn’t traditionally famous for naturals (it built its reputation on ultra-clean washed coffees), but in recent years, producers like Gitwe have been experimenting more. The result is coffees like this—still structured and elegant, but with a playful, fruit-driven twist that stands out on a menu.

products.title: Indonesia Sumatra Kenyalang G1
products.body_html:
Roast: Medium–Dark (balanced body, deep sweetness, low bitterness)
Process: Wet-Hulled
Taste Notes: Molasses • Dark Chocolate • Brown Sugar
Profile: Lasting • Bold • Full-bodied

Roaster Notes

Roasted to enhance body and depth, highlighting the natural richness of the wet-hulled process. Expect a thick mouthfeel, low acidity, and a strong, lingering aftertaste. Excellent as a black coffee or for those who prefer a robust, traditional profile.

A powerful and deeply satisfying cup from Sumatra. This G1 wet-hulled coffee from DP Kenyalang delivers rich molasses sweetness, layered with dark chocolate and brown sugar depth. The body is heavy and coating, with a long, lingering finish that defines a classic strong Indonesian profile.

Bean Info

Grown in Indonesia’s highland regions and processed using the traditional wet-hulled (Giling Basah) method, this Sumatra coffee is known for its unmistakable intensity. Earthy sweetness unfolds into notes of molasses and dark chocolate, while brown sugar rounds the cup with warmth and weight. Bold, grounding, and long-lasting — this is coffee for those who appreciate strength and depth over brightness.

products.title: Brazil Castanhas Do Brazil
products.body_html:
Roast: Medium
Varietal: Mundo Novo, Catuai
Process: Natural
Altitude: 900 - 1,100 M
Taste note:
Black: Nutty, Milk Chocolate, Dried Fruit, Creamy
Latte: Peanut Candy, Toffee, Chocolate Praline, Biscoff

Roaster Note
True to its name—Castanhas meaning "nuts" in Portuguese—this Brazilian lot is a quintessential daily drinker. It offers a classic flavor profile dominated by roasted nuts and creamy milk chocolate. The mixed natural processing enhances its body and brings a subtle, jammy dried-fruit sweetness to the finish. As a medium-dark roast, it is incredibly balanced and low in acidity, making it the perfect foundation for a rich espresso or a comforting, traditional filter brew.

Bean Info
"Castanhas do Brazil" is a curated selection from established farms across the Cerrado Mineiro and Mogiana regions, known for their flat plateaus and consistent climate. The "Mixed Natural" designation refers to the traditional Brazilian method of sun-drying cherries, which imparts a heavy body and deep sweetness to the bean. These regions utilize advanced harvesting and sorting techniques to ensure a "Fine Cup" quality, resulting in a coffee that is exceptionally consistent and versatile for specialty roasteries.

products.title: El Salvador El Borbollon
products.body_html:
Roast: Medium Dark Roast
Varietal: Red Bourbon
Process: Washed
Altitude: 1,350 M
Region: Santa Ana, El Salvador
Producer: Finca Lima (Lima family)
Taste note:
Black: Red Apple, Yellow Fruit, Dolce, Clean
Latte: Milk Chocolate, Dolce, Hazelnut

Roaster Note
Produced by the renowned Lima family in the Santa Ana region, this washed Red Bourbon offers a classic and transparent profile. Expect a cup defined by its structured sweetness and clear fruit notes, particularly red apple and vibrant yellow fruits. The careful, traditional washing process and sun-drying on patios for two to three weeks result in a coffee that is exceptionally consistent. It serves as a versatile selection—refreshing and bright as a filter brew, while maintaining a smooth, "dolce" sweetness that pairs perfectly with milk.

Bean Info
Finca Lima represents over a century of coffee-growing expertise by the Lima family, situated on the volcanic slopes near the Santa Ana Volcano. Rather than a single estate, the name serves as an umbrella for multiple family-run farms focused on quality and long-term land stewardship. These coffees are grown under native shade trees at high elevations, which creates a stable microclimate and allows cherries to ripen slowly. This slower maturation, combined with the nutrient-rich volcanic soil, contributes to the excellent bean density and balanced acidity found in this 2025 crop.

products.title: Berry Gummy Blend
products.body_html:
This espresso blend brings together the best of Ethiopia’s two processing styles—washed and natural—to create a cup that’s both vibrant and balanced. The washed component contributes clarity, bright citrus, and floral tea-like notes, while the natural component adds layers of ripe berries, jammy sweetness, and tropical fruit depth.

Roasted with espresso in mind, the blend strikes a balance between fruit-forward complexity and a smooth, syrupy body. As a straight shot, it’s juicy and expressive; with milk, the berry sweetness folds into a creamy, almost dessert-like cup. A lively, modern espresso that showcases Ethiopia’s versatility.

products.title: Honeycomb Coconut Blend
products.body_html:
Taste Notes: Honeycomb • Coconut Sugar • Caramel Milk
Origin: Ethiopia & Colombia

Roaster’s Note

Inspired by the aroma of freshly baked coconut cake, this blend brings together the bright sweetness of Ethiopian coffee and the creamy body of Colombian beans. Brewed as a black coffee, it shows a clear honeycomb sweetness with lively citrus hints. When paired with milk, the cup transforms into a silky caramel-milk dessert layered with subtle coconut notes. A warm, golden cup designed for everyday comfort.

products.title: Ethiopia Kayon Mountain Lot 40
products.body_html:
Origin: Guji, Ethiopia
District / Zone: Shakiso
Locality: Taro & Sewana
Producer: Ismael Hassen Aredo
Altitude: 1,900–2,200 masl
Varietals: 74110, 74112
Process: Natural
Tasting Notes: Mango • Blueberries • Mandarin

Roaster’s Note

Roasted to emphasize the silky mango body and the bright, berry-driven acidity. Blueberries come through clearly as the cup cools, while the mandarin note gives a refreshing citrus snap. Best as filter; also shines as a modern, fruity espresso.


About this lot

Kayon Mountain Coffee stands as one of Ethiopia’s rare, truly vertically integrated, family-owned estates—a remarkable exception in a country where coffee production is usually fragmented among thousands of smallholders. Founded in 2012 by Ismael Hassen Aredo and his family, the estate spans nearly 500 hectares in the highlands of the Guji Zone, with 300 hectares dedicated to coffee and the remainder preserved as native forest.

From the beginning, the family envisioned a farm that blends quality, sustainability, and community upliftment. Kayon Mountain is certified organic, biodynamic, and shade-grown, applying natural composting and biodiversity preservation to cultivate its cherries at 1,900–2,200 masl.

More than just a coffee farm, Kayon Mountain provides fair wages, healthcare, transportation, and stable employment for over 300 seasonal workers and 25 full-time staff, offering a dignified alternative to the region’s mining jobs.

Unlike most farms in Ethiopia, Kayon Mountain also owns its own wet mill and dry mill, giving it full control over every step—from harvesting to drying to export. This rare level of traceability and processing oversight allows Kayon Mountain to consistently produce clean, expressive coffees while bypassing the Ethiopian Commodity Exchange to sell directly to specialty buyers around the world.

Kayon Mountain is more than an origin—it’s a model for what Ethiopian coffee can become when heritage, sustainability, and family vision align.

products.title: Ethiopia Uraga Nigusse Nare Murango Lot Q
products.body_html:
Varieties: 74158, 74112
Process: Natural
Elevation: 2,100 MASL
Taste Notes: Prune • Concord Grape • Lingon Berries

Roaster’s Note

This medium-light roast brings out the juicy sweetness and clean fruit structure classic to high-altitude Uraga naturals, while adding a touch of warmth and roundness to the cup.

Expect a soft opening of stewed prune and dark berries, followed by a vibrant but controlled concord grape acidity — more like grape compote than sharp tartness. The medium-light development enhances the coffee’s natural sweetness, giving it a silky, honey-like body without sacrificing clarity.

As the cup cools, delicate lingon berry brightness lifts the finish, offering a refreshing, lightly tannic snap reminiscent of a young red wine. This profile shines as filter, but also produces expressive modern espresso with jammy fruit and a clean aftertaste.


About this lot

Up in the high, forested slopes of Uraga in Ethiopia’s Guji Zone, farmer Nigusse Nare cultivates coffee on 6 hectares of land passed down through generations. At 2,100 meters, his trees grow slowly under native shade, enriching the cherries with dense sugars and aromatic complexity.

Nigusse farms using traditional, organic practices — compost, mulch, and natural soil stewardship. Coffee has been central to his family’s life for decades, and today he continues the legacy with the help of his wife and children.

In recent seasons, Nigusse began separating small microlots like this Murango Lot to improve traceability and highlight the unique character of his farm. Through collaboration with local agronomists and exporter partners, he has refined his processing and achieved exceptional cup quality.

Despite challenges — unpredictable weather, rising farming costs, and limited infrastructure — Nigusse remains committed to producing some of the region’s most expressive natural coffees. This lot reflects the resilience, craft, and deep-rooted coffee heritage of Ethiopia’s smallholder farmers.

products.title: Colombia Wuchii Cauca Popayan Reserve
products.body_html:
Roast: Medium–Dark (balanced body, deep sweetness, low bitterness)
Process: Washed
Variety: Caturra / Castillo / Colombia
Altitude: 1,700–1,900 masl
Region: Popayán, Cauca
Brewing method: Filter / Espresso
Goes well with milk?: Yes
Tasting note: Dark Caramel · Roasted Almond · Cocoa Nibs · Gentle Citrus Lift

Roaster Notes

During profiling, we pushed development just enough to bring out caramelized sweetness, cocoa depth, and a rounded body, while keeping bitterness low and acidity gentle.

The beans from Popayán are naturally dense, so they respond well to heat. We extended the Maillard phase to build a rich, warm nutty tone, then finished with a controlled development time to preserve a subtle citrus lift that keeps the cup lively.

Expect a cup that is smooth, balanced, and dependable—a comforting Colombian profile elevated by careful roasting. Excellent as espresso, crowd-pleasing as a milk coffee, and beautifully clean on filter despite its fuller roast.


Bean Info

In the mountains surrounding Popayán, 3000 farmers of the Wuchii collective cultivate coffee on nutrient-rich volcanic soil, benefiting from cool nights and steady rainfall. These slow-growing conditions produce cherries with concentrated sugars—perfect for a medium–dark roast profile.

While many darker roasts tend to lose nuance, Popayán coffees are prized for their structure and density, allowing them to withstand deeper roasting without becoming ashy or bitter. This is why we selected this reserve lot: its natural sweetness and washed-process clarity remain intact even as the roast reaches a fuller, more developed stage.

The result is a cup that feels familiar yet elevated—comforting like a traditional Colombian brew, but cleaner, smoother, and fuller-bodied. Expect rich caramelization, nutty warmth, and a persistent cocoa finish that pairs beautifully with milk or stands confidently on its own.

products.title: Ethiopia Gori Forest Wild Geisha
products.body_html:
Farm: Gori Gesha Forest
Variety: Wild Gesha
Process: Natural (sun-dried)
Altitude: 1,900–2,100 m
Tasting Notes: blueberry, grape juice, rose, mixed berries, bergamot, lime (with a peach-like sweetness)


Roaster’s Note
This year’s harvest from Gori Gesha is as wonderful as ever. In the cup we found a clean, floral profile with abundant berries, peach-like sweetness, and bright bergamot—a standout natural-processed Wild Gesha. A must-have for fruit-forward coffee lovers.


About this lot
Ethiopia is the birthplace of Gesha. The Gesha cultivated in Ethiopia isn’t the same genetic line as Panama Geisha. In Ethiopia, “Gesha” commonly refers to three selections:

  • Gori Gesha (GG): selections replicated from the genetic diversity found in the Gori Gesha coffee forest.
  • Illubabor Forest 1974 (IF): discovered during a 1974 survey in the Illubabor forest and later developed by Ethiopia’s agricultural research center for disease resistance.
  • Gesha 1931 (G31): forest selections named for their plant characteristics, bean appearance/screen size, and cup profile—very similar sensorially to Panama Geisha.

products.title: Colombia La Julia Chocolate Ice Cream
products.body_html:
Region: Trujillo, Valle Del Cauca
Farm: La Julia Estate
Altitude: 1650 ~ 1750 M
Varietal: Colombia
Process: Washed
Flavor Notes: Chocolate ice cream, sugarcane, orange, nuts, dark chocolate, black cherry
Brewing method: Filter / Espresso
Goes well with milk?: Yes

Roaster Notes
I gave this coffee a medium-dark roast to bring out its full body and tone down the acidity. In the cup, you’ll find rich, dark chocolate coating the palate, with a sweetness that reminds me of chocolate ice cream and a hint of cherry jam on top.

It makes for a bold, chocolaty latte and a satisfying, full-bodied americano—an easy daily cup for just about anyone.

 

Bean Info
La Julia Estate is a family-run farm located in the lush highlands of Quindío, Colombia—an iconic region known for producing clean, vibrant coffees. Grown at elevations of 1,500–1,700 masl, this lot features the Colombia varietal, fully washed to bring out its clarity and structure.

La Julia is Rainforest Alliance certified, which reflects the farm’s ongoing commitment to sustainability. The estate follows environmentally responsible practices—protecting native forest cover, managing water use carefully, and supporting the welfare of farm workers and surrounding communities.

products.title: Brazil Pinhal Topazio
products.body_html:
Farm/Producer: Fazenda Pinhal / Pedro Gabarra Teixeira

Location: Sul de Minas, Minas Gerais

Varietal: Topazio

Process: Natural

Altitude: 950 - 1,150 masl

Roaster Note
This Topazio lot from Fazenda Pinhal in Brazil was naturally processed to bring out its rich sweetness and comforting depth. I roasted it to a balanced medium, allowing the creamy hazelnut and smooth baker’s chocolate notes to take center stage, while a gentle dried apricot fruitiness adds a touch of brightness to the cup.

The result is a coffee that’s approachable yet layered: nutty and chocolaty enough to satisfy those who love a classic daily brew, but with just enough dried fruit nuance to keep it interesting. As espresso or filter, it’s a smooth, medium-bodied cup. With milk, the chocolate deepens and the hazelnut turns creamy, creating a comforting latte.


Bean Info:
Fazenda Pinhal and is owned by Pedro, João, and Milau Gabarra, sixth generation coffee farmers, who have directed the farm to focus heavily on sustainability and the farming of high grade speciality coffee.

They are hugely respected within the specialty coffee industry both for their excellent coffee quality and also their commitment to sustainability, having won the most sustainable farm in Brazil back in 2019, after moving 100% of its energy to renewable sourced with solar panels on the farm and in 2020 became CarbonNeutral®.

Around 35% of their 914 hectare farm is planted for coffee with the remainder being left either as untouched natural reserve or for any of the various reforestation initiatives being carried out by the family. These include a Eucalyptus forest, a 20ha native forest redevelopment and a rehabilitation and release sanctuary for native birds.

products.title: Brazil Carrancas Microlot
products.body_html:
Farm/Producer: Carrancas / Joao Osvaldo

Location: Lavras, South of Minas

Varietal: Yellow Bourbon

Process: Natural

Altitude: 1,000 MASL

Roaster Note
This microlot from Carrancas, Brazil is all about comfort and creaminess. I roasted it to bring out a soft oat milk fragrance with a gentle pecan-like nuttiness that lingers in the cup. As black, it’s smooth and mellow, with a creamy body and low acidity that makes it easy to drink. Add milk, and the nutty character deepens into a pecan-cream sweetness, creating a silky, balanced latte that feels both indulgent and approachable.


Bean Info:
Fazenda Pinhal and is owned by Pedro, João, and Milau Gabarra, sixth generation coffee farmers, who have directed the farm to focus heavily on sustainability and the farming of high grade speciality coffee.

They are hugely respected within the specialty coffee industry both for their excellent coffee quality and also their commitment to sustainability, having won the most sustainable farm in Brazil back in 2019, after moving 100% of its energy to renewable sourced with solar panels on the farm and in 2020 became CarbonNeutral®.

Around 35% of their 914 hectare farm is planted for coffee with the remainder being left either as untouched natural reserve or for any of the various reforestation initiatives being carried out by the family. These include a Eucalyptus forest, a 20ha native forest redevelopment and a rehabilitation and release sanctuary for native birds.

products.title: Panama Mama Cata Irma Geisha (Natural)
products.body_html:
Region: Boquete
Altitude: 1500-1700m
Processing: Natural
Taste Note: Floral, Peach, Berries, Stone fruits, Melon
Brewing Method: Filter
Goes well with milk? Yes - if you like lightly floralish with caramel milk based coffee

Roaster Note:

This natural-processed Geisha from Mama Cata Estate bursts with vibrant fruit and florals. In the cup, expect berries and peach note, and jasmine-like aromatics, carried by a silky texture and lively sweetness. As it cools, layers of stone fruit and honey emerge, adding depth and elegance.

I gave it a light roast to preserve its expressive fruit character while keeping the cup clean and balanced. The result is a coffee that’s both exotic and refined—playful in its fruitiness, yet unmistakably Geisha in its clarity and grace.

 

Bean Info
Mama Cata Estate: Established in 1959 and managed by the Garrido family, it's located at 1,500-1,700 meters above sea level and known for quality improvements implemented by current owner Jose David Garrido Perez.

Irma Estate: A newer Garrido family estate in El Salto, Boquete (1,350-1,400m), specializing in high-quality coffee through meticulous processing.

products.title: Colombia La Luisa Pacamara
products.body_html:
Country: Colombia
Region: Antioquia
Farm: La Luisa
Variety: Pacamara
Process: Natural
Altitude: 1,850 MASL
Producer: Juan Pablo Velez
Brewing Method: Filter


Roaster Note
This is a truly unique-tasting coffee, showcasing the distinct character of the Pacamara variety.

When hot, it opens up with a gentle herbal tone and a hint of roasted coconut shreds — complex yet comforting.

As it cools, the herbal note gracefully fades, giving way to sweet fruit tones reminiscent of stone fruits and tropical fruits.

The result is a mellow, pleasantly sweet, and delicious cup — layered and evolving with every sip.

A sweet ecoffee that’s hard to forget.


Bean Info
La Luisa Estate is located in a small town called Bolívar in the southwest of Antioquia. The Vélez family has been growing coffee here since 1907, cultivating varieties such as Caturra, Castillo, Maragogipe, Pacamara, Tabi, Gesha, and Colombia. The current generation remains passionate and energetic about coffee, committed to producing high-quality, traceable green coffee beans.


Pacamara was little known at first—it was developed in 1958, but due to its low yield and the difficulty of processing its large beans, it remained under the radar for half a century. Then, in a stunning comeback, Pacamara won dual championships at the Cup of Excellence competitions in both Guatemala and Honduras, even sweeping the top three spots in El Salvador. In the years that followed, it consistently ranked among the top in major coffee competitions. It is now hailed as a rising star on par with Gesha.


Pacamara combines the floral and fruity notes of Pacas with the rich, rounded body of Maragogipe, making it a rare and naturally gifted variety. However, due to its genetic instability, it requires careful cultivation and skilled farming, and its yield has always remained relatively low.

products.title: Cotton Candy Blend
products.body_html:
The blend is a combination of Brazil, Guatemala and Ethiopia.

The Brazil coffee provides a sweet nutty notes, providing a pleasant foundation for the blend. The Ethiopian coffees are roasted to a slightly lighter profile to preserve their fruitiness and sweetness. The Guatemala coffee also adds in a pleasant floral and tea like characteristics.

The overall flavor profile is a mix of berries, chocolate, roasted almonds, and caramel sweetness. When paired with milk, you can taste butterscotch, cotton candy base, and milk tea.

Despite the medium-dark roast level, the blend still has a complex and interesting flavor profile.

products.title: Guatemala Bella Carmona
products.body_html:
Roaster Note

This coffee surprised me with just how sweet and fragrant it is. From the first sip, there’s a hints of lycheethat carries through the cup, adding a delicate and refreshing lift. As it opens up, the sweetness deepens into something reminiscent of raisins, but with an added layer of floral fruitiness that gives it extra vibrancy.

The cup is smooth, juicy, and memorable—balancing natural sweetness with a gentle fruity complexity. It’s the kind of coffee that feels both familiar and exotic at the same time, offering comfort with a playful twist.


Bean Info
Guatemala Bella Carmona coffee beans originate from the esteemed Antigua region, renowned for its rich volcanic soil and ideal climate conditions that contribute to exceptional coffee quality. This coffee is cultivated by small-scale farmers on the slopes of Volcán de Agua, with cherries processed at the Bella Vista Mill, ensuring meticulous attention to detail and a commitment to excellence. 

The beans undergo a traditional washed processing method, where the fruit skin and pulp are removed before drying. This technique enhances the coffee's clarity and brightness. The medium-light roast profile highlights the inherent characteristics of the Bourbon and Caturra varietals, resulting in a balanced and nuanced cup.

Tasting notes for Guatemala Bella Carmona include lychee, cherry syrup, and raisin, offering a sweet and fruity flavor profile. The coffee's bright acidity and smooth body make it a delightful choice for those seeking a vibrant and well-rounded brew.

products.title: Ethiopia Arbegona Duwancho G1
products.body_html:
Producer: Nigusse Gemeda Mude
Region: Arbegona
Varietal: 74158
Altitude: 2280-2360M
Processing Station: Duwancho
Process: Natural
Taste Profile: Yellow floral, Mango, Pineapple, Apricot, Bergamot

Roaster Note: 
Sweet and fruit‑driven, this classic Ethiopian natural opens with a sweet ripe mango and a hint of dried pineapple. As the cup cools, tropical fruits like mango compote and ripe blackberry—rounded out by a playful orange‑candy finish. Versatile and forgiving, it shines in every brew method from filter to espresso, and its vivid fruit layers meld beautifully with milk for an indulgent flat white or cappuccino.


Beans info:
Arbegona‑Duwancho Natural G1 is prized for its extreme altitude, tight JARC genetics, and meticulous raised‑bed drying – yielding ultra‑dense, small seeds that roast evenly and erupt with red‑berry, tropical and floral character. If you want a show‑stopping Ethiopian natural to anchor seasonal single‑origins or competition espresso, this lot delivers both cup vibrancy and traceable, ethical sourcing.

products.title: Strawberry Milkshake Blend
products.body_html:
Roaster Notes:

A fine blend of Ethiopian natural-processed beans, bringing sweet fruit notes, and Colombian yeast-fermented washed beans that highlight vibrant strawberry.

Enjoyed black (filter or Americano), it reveals layers of berry jam and fruit tea—best sipped hot or warm, as the flavors fade when cold. With milk, the coffee truly shines: think strawberry waffle biscuit, creamy milkshake, and sweet milk in every sip.

products.title: Colombia Finca La Luisa Strawberry
products.body_html:
Origin: Antioquia, Colombia
Producer: Finca La Luisa
Variety: Caturra
Process: Strawberry Fermentation Honey
Altitude: 1,600 – 1,750 masl
Roast Level: Light to Medium-Light
Cup Profile: Strawberry jam, red apple, rose petal, creamy sweetness

Roaster Note

Opening with the aroma of strawberry preserves and rose petals, this coffee blooms into a cup of red apple acidity and creamy, honey-like texture. The sweetness is deep yet elegant, reminiscent of fruit compote and vanilla cream.

A light-medium roast preserves its delicate aromatics while rounding the acidity for a balanced, juicy profile. 

 

Bean Info

Perched among the misty ridges of Antioquia, Finca La Luisa has become a symbol of Colombia’s experimental coffee movement. Guided by a deep curiosity for fermentation science, the farm’s producers have developed a series of fruit-infused honey processes designed to amplify natural sweetness and aroma.

For this lot, ripe Caturra cherries are fermented with fresh strawberries in a controlled anaerobic environment. The fruit sugars interact with the coffee’s own mucilage, creating a slow, layered fermentation that infuses the beans with subtle berry esters and floral tones. After fermentation, the cherries are partially honey-dried on raised beds, allowing the coffee to retain both its clean structure and its vivid fruit perfume.

The result is a cup that embodies Antioquia’s innovative spirit—bright, fragrant, and indulgently sweet—bridging traditional craftsmanship with modern flavor experimentation.

products.title: Colombia La Piragua Alexander Vargas Pink Bourbon
products.body_html:
Origin: Huila, Colombia
Producer: Alexander Vargas, Finca La Piragua
Variety: Pink Bourbon
Process: Washed
Altitude: 1,750 – 1,900 masl
Roast Level: Medium Light
Cup Profile: Dried cranberries, grapefruit, tangerine, floral finish

Roaster Note

This coffee opens with a bright and lively aroma, leading into a flavor profile layered with dried cranberries, grapefruit, and sweet tangerine. The acidity is sparkling yet balanced, giving the cup a refreshing and juicy structure.

The light roast approach brings out the distinct Pink Bourbon character — a mix of sweetness and citrus clarity — while maintaining a silky, tea-like mouthfeel. As the coffee cools, delicate floral and honey undertones unfold, adding complexity to its clean finish.

Ideal for pour-over or hand brew, this lot delivers a vibrant, fruit-driven cup with a refined and uplifting aftertaste — a showcase of Colombia’s terroir and the meticulous craftsmanship of Alexander Vargas.

Bean Info

High in the lush mountains of Huila, Colombia, sits Finca La Piragua, a small family-run farm managed by Alexander Vargas. The farm lies between 1,750 and 1,900 meters above sea level — a region blessed with cool mountain air, rich volcanic soil, and year-round rainfall, ideal for slow cherry maturation and concentrated sweetness.

The Pink Bourbon variety is a rare mutation of Red and Yellow Bourbon, known for its translucent pink cherries and refined cup character. This hybrid thrives in Huila’s microclimate, where warm days and cool nights encourage the development of complex fruit sugars and crisp acidity.

After selective handpicking, the cherries are fermented for 24–36 hours, then fully washed and sun-dried on raised beds to ensure a clean and transparent expression. This careful process highlights Pink Bourbon’s signature clarity and citrus brightness, delivering a cup that bursts with dried cranberry sweetness, grapefruit zest, and tangerine juiciness.

Each harvest from La Piragua represents Alexander’s commitment to precision, sustainability, and flavor purity — a shining example of how smallholder farmers in Huila continue to redefine Colombia’s specialty coffee landscape.

products.title: Costa Rica Los Tucanes Don Mayo Geisha
products.body_html:
Origin: Tarrazú, Costa Rica
Producer: Don Mayo Micromill
Variety: Geisha
Process: Red Honey
Altitude: 1,800 – 2,000 masl
Roast Level: Light to Medium-Light
Cup Profile: Red berries, fruit candy, subtle floral, honey sweetness

Roaster Note

This Geisha opens with an aromatic bouquet of wildflowers and red berries, followed by a juicy sweetness reminiscent of fruit candy and ripe cherries. As the cup cools, a silky honey texture emerges, layered with delicate florals and a whisper of citrus zest.

The roast was intentionally kept light to medium-light to highlight the varietal’s signature clarity and the vivid fruit expression brought out by the red honey process. Expect a clean finish with lingering sweetness and elegant floral aftertones — a cup that evolves gracefully with each sip.

Brew it as a pour-over or filter to appreciate its clarity and fragrance, or use single-origin espresso for a candy-like fruit shot with a smooth, syrupy body.


Bean Info

The Don Mayo Micromill is one of Tarrazú’s most renowned producers, known for meticulous processing and clean, expressive coffees. This Geisha variety, grown at high altitude, develops intense fruit character and floral complexity. The Red Honey process strikes a perfect balance between natural and washed—preserving sweetness and fruit clarity while maintaining a smooth, refined body.

products.title: Costa Rica Brunca Rivense El Mango
products.body_html:
Region: Tarrazú, Costa Rica
Farm: El Mango
Producer: Rivense Micromill
Varietal: Caturra / Red Catuai
Process: Black Honey (high mucilage retention during drying)
Altitude: 1,400 – 1,700 masl
Taste Note: Hazelnut-chocolate smoothness, dark fruit depth, winey nuance, black tea finish
Roast Level: Medium
Brewing method: Filter or Espresso

Roaster Note
This El Mango Black Honey opens with refined hazelnut-chocolate notes that set a comforting foundation. As the cup evolves, hints of dark fruits—think black cherry and plum—emerge with layered complexity, while a subtle winey nuance surfaces, adding intrigue. The texture is smooth and velvety, bridging the sweetness and depth harmoniously. In the finish, a clean black tea aftertaste lingers, providing structural balance and clarity. The medium roast highlights all these elements — fruit, sweetness, body — while ensuring the finish stays elegant.

Bean Info

Finca El Mango is an 8-hectare specialty coffee estate located in the Brunca region (valleys of Chirripó) in southern Costa Rica, run by the Ureña-Rojas family. The farm uses the micromill Rivense del Chirripó to process cherries from their own land. 

In this lot, they employ a Black Honey process — meaning a large portion of the mucilage is kept on the bean during drying, amplifying sweetness, body, and complexity. 

The cherries are carefully selected for ripeness, dry-pulped (i.e., removal of skin but leaving mucilage), and then laid on raised beds in the sun for an extended period (around 12–15 days) under close monitoring to avoid over-fermentation or rot. 

The Brunca / Chirripó microclimate — lying between high peaks like Cerro de la Muerte and Cerro Chirripó — offers altitude, temperature variation, and fresh mountain air. 

These conditions, combined with the Black Honey approach, produce coffees with rich sweetness, deep fruit complexity, and structural clarity.

This lot has risen in reputation in the region; Finca El Mango is one of the few estates in Brunca pioneering specialty and honey processing methods in an area not historically known for it.

products.title: Panama Boquete Elida ASD Catuai
products.body_html:
Region: Boquete, Chiriquí, Panama
Producer: Elida Estate (Lamastus family)
Varietal: Catuai
Process: ASD (Anaerobic Slow Dry) Natural
Altitude: 1,670 – 1,825 masl
Taste Note: Tropical fruit, sweet orange, dried pineapple, fruit liqueur, berry sweetness, cherry-chocolate, juicy fruit tea, lingering brown sugar

Roaster Note

This Elida ASD Catuai is a tropical and indulgent cup from the very first sip. Aromas of pineapple and fruit liqueur set the stage, followed by lively sweet orange and berry sweetness on the palate. Layers of cherry-chocolate richness intertwine with a refreshing juicy fruit tea quality, giving the cup both depth and lift. The texture is smooth and rounded, while the aftertaste lingers with an elegant brown sugar sweetness that grows more intense as it cools. This is a coffee that combines vibrancy with comfort — tropical brightness, confectionery richness, and a finish that resonates long after drinking.


Bean info

Elida Estate, owned by the Lamastus family, is one of Panama’s most iconic coffee producers, renowned for both its Cup of Excellence performances and its pioneering processing methods. The farm sits on the slopes of Volcán Barú, partly within a national park, where cool mountain air, volcanic soils, and high elevation slow cherry maturation and concentrate sweetness.

This lot is processed with the ASD (Anaerobic Slow Dry) Natural method. Ripe cherries are first sealed in oxygen-limited tanks to ferment in their own juices, developing layered aromatics, before undergoing a carefully controlled slow-drying stage that can last up to two months. The method enhances fruit intensity, complexity, and long sweetness while preserving clarity.

The result is a coffee that balances tropical vibrancy with sugar-rich depth: a cup that feels lush yet refined, showing both the terroir of Boquete and the innovation of the Lamastus family.

products.title: Ethiopia Guji Urabeast G1
products.body_html:
Region: Guji, Oromia, Ethiopia
Producer: Smallholder farmers (Uraga area, processed at Urabeast lot)
Varietal: Ethiopian Heirloom (including JARC 74110, 74112)
Process: Washed
Altitude: 2,100 – 2,300 masl
Taste Note: Red currant, grape, tea-like finish
Brewing method: Best as pour over (V60, Kalita, Origami) for clarity; also works in lighter espresso

Roaster Note
This Urabeast lot bursts with a lively brightness of red currant, unfolding into juicy layers of grape sweetness. The washed process keeps the flavors clean and defined, allowing the fruit character to shine with remarkable clarity. As the cup settles, a gentle red tea aftertaste emerges, soft and lingering, bringing balance to its vibrant acidity. The texture is silky yet light, with a finish that carries both elegance and persistence. Each sip feels refreshing and precise, embodying the hallmark refinement of Guji coffees while standing out for its structured fruit depth.

Bean Info
The Urabeast lot is a specialty microlot from the Uraga / Guji area in southern Ethiopia. The name “Urabeast” is a coined lot name combining “Uraga” (the local region) with “beast,” meant to evoke energy and strength. The coffee is sourced from smallholder farmers in micro-regions such as Tobutu, Gomoro, and Suke around Uraga.

While Ethiopian coffees generally remain grouped under “heirloom” or local landraces, this lot is believed to contain a mix of local varieties, including JARC-74 lines (74110, 74112) and inherited indigenous varietals passed through farmer generations. Such diversity contributes to layered aromatics and complexity in Ethiopian coffees.

This lot is fully washed. The cherries are hand-picked and delivered fresh, sorted and floated to remove defective or low-quality fruit. The pulping is done promptly, and the beans undergo fermentation (wet/soaked) to remove mucilage completely. After fermentation, the beans are washed and then dried on raised beds under controlled conditions — turned periodically to ensure even drying and to avoid over-fermentation or undesired off-flavors.

At altitudes between ~2,100 and 2,300 masl, the region experiences cool nights and high diurnal temperature variation, which slows cherry maturation and intensifies the development of sugars and aromatic precursors. The soils and microclimate of Guji, combined with careful processing, allow the lot to express both vibrant fruit notes and deeper complexity.

The Urabeast lot is positioned as a bold, distinctive microlot within Guji’s growing reputation for expressive, terroir-driven coffees. Its name and branding evoke strength, yet the microlot aims to preserve the elegance and nuance typical of Ethiopian washed profiles. The mix of heirloom genetics and precise washing/drying contribute to clarity, depth, and a fruit-driven cup with red-tea character.

products.title: Ethiopia Gedeo Yirgacheffe Konga Amederaro G1
products.body_html:
Region: Yirgacheffe, Gedeo Zone, Ethiopia
Producer: Konga Amederaro Washing Station with smallholder farmers
Varietal: Ethiopian Heirloom / Local landraces (incl. JARC selections)
Process: Washed
Altitude: ~2,000 masl
Taste Note: Wild berries, blood orange, green grape, black tea with long finish 

Roaster Note
This Konga Amederaro lot welcomes you with an elegant tapestry of wild berries and blood orange, each sip layered with green grape accents and a soft whisper of black tea. The washed process gives clarity, letting fruit and tea notes shine without muddiness. The finish is long and refined, leaving a gentle tea-like aftertaste that lingers as a calming echo. On the palate, brightness, floral lift, and restrained sweetness play in harmony — a coffee that feels both vivid and poised, inviting contemplation in each cup.


Bean Info

Konga Amederaro is a washing station in the Konga village (Amederaro kebele) of Yirgacheffe, in the Gedeo Zone, which works with many local smallholder farmers to process their coffee cherries.

 The region is known for its high-altitude, cool climate and well-drained soils, providing ideal conditions for specialty coffee development. 

In this lot, fully washed processing is applied: cherries are delivered to the station, sorted, depulped, fermented under controlled conditions, washed, and then dried (often on raised beds) to preserve clarity and clean fruit character. 

The Konga station has earned recognition for its strict quality controls, having placed in competitions and is regarded as one of the consistent high-quality producers in Yirgacheffe. 

Farmers in the area frequently maintain “garden coffee” plots — small plots around their homes — growing heirloom varieties. Shade trees, organic composting, and minimal chemical inputs are often part of the local practices (many producers are “passive organic” due to low access to chemical farming aids). 

The washed processing allows the floral and tea-like qualities typical of Yirgacheffe coffees to stand in relief, while still revealing the fruit brightness and complexity of the local varietals under careful handling.

products.title: Colombia Huila El Silencio Red Pink Bourbon
products.body_html:
Region: Palestina, Huila, Colombia
Producer: María Rodríguez / El Silencio Red
Varietal: Pink Bourbon
Process: Washed (dual-phase fermentation)
Altitude: 1,700 – 2,200 masl 
Taste Note: Cherry, red grape, molasses 

Roaster Note

This El Silencio Pink Bourbon greets you with a vibrant burst of red fruits and red grape, layered with a bright citrus edge like blood orange. Beneath that sits a gentle floral whisper that lingers mid-palate, while a touch of molasses sweetness anchors the finish. The dual fermentation gives the cup body and depth without sacrificing clarity — flavors dance cleanly across the palate rather than muddying each other. Each sip is juicy and expressive, inviting exploration of its layers. It's a refined, bold coffee that delivers both brightness and substance in harmony.


Bean Info

El Silencio Red is a microlot from María Rodríguez, a third-generation coffee producer in Palestina, Huila, Colombia. 

She took over after her father’s passing and continues his legacy by emphasizing quality, innovation, and varietal exploration. 
On her farm, she has introduced varieties like Pink Bourbon, Gesha, and SL28. 

The Pink Bourbon beans are grown at high altitude (1,700–2,200 masl), where cool nights and a stable mountain microclimate favor slow cherry maturation and aromatic development. 

For processing, El Silencio uses a dual-phase washed fermentation method: first, cherries undergo an anaerobic or submerged fermentation (12–24 hours) while whole, absorbing skin and mucilage influence. Then cherries are pulped, and a second fermentation (18–24 hours) is done with the mucilage intact in open tanks. After fermentation, they are fully washed and dried on raised beds under controlled conditions to preserve clarity and avoid defects. 

This processing style achieves a balance — combining the precision and cleanliness of washed coffees with the deeper fruit complexity that fermentation can bring. The result is an expressive, juicy, and layered cup, with red fruit brightness, floral overtones, and depth from molasses notes.

products.title: Peru Los Santos Geisha (Honey)
products.body_html:
Region: Cusco, Peru
Producer: Los Santos smallholder farmers
Varietal: Geisha
Process: Honey
Altitude: 1,700 – 1,900 masl
Taste Note: Floral, Berry, Peach, Lychee sweetness

Roaster Note

This honey-processed Geisha opens with a graceful bouquet of floral aromatics, delicate yet expressive. The first sip reveals layers of berry brightness intertwined with soft peach juiciness, evolving into a refined sweetness reminiscent of fresh lychee. The body is light and tea-like, carrying the fruit and floral interplay with elegance and clarity. Each sip feels balanced yet dynamic, with a sweetness that lingers gently on the palate. The honey process deepens the fruit notes while preserving the hallmark purity of Geisha, resulting in a cup that is both vibrant and soothing — perfect for slow, mindful enjoyment.


Bean info

Finca Los Santos is a family-run estate in the Amazonas region of Peru, with a coffee heritage dating back to 1941. Over generations, the Santos family has refined their cultivation of various varieties — including Caturra, Bourbon, Pacas — and more recently Geisha (Gesha). Some lots are designated “Green Tip Geisha,” meaning beans show slight green tinges or tip coloration during the cherry stage.

In their honey-processed Geisha lots, Los Santos leaves a portion of the mucilage intact after pulping, rather than fully washing it away. This retained mucilage acts like a protective “honey” layer during drying, imparting natural sugars, body, and depth. For more intense “Red Honey / Black Honey” style lots, more mucilage is retained and drying is slower, with careful raking or turning to prevent defects. For example, in their COE Red Honey Green Tip Geisha, beans are dried in solar parabolic dryers over ~2 weeks, and are raked every ~3 hours to ensure uniform drying. 

On Los Santos, mucilage management, micro-climate control (shade, airflow), and timing of drying are critical. The estate also practices intercropping (banana, yuca, corn) and avoids synthetic pesticides, relying instead on ecological pest control and soil management methods. 

The terroir — high elevation, cooler nights, volcanic and organic soils — gives slow cherry maturation. The honey process acts as a bridge between natural and washed: preserving fruit complexity and sweetness while maintaining clarity. In good honey-Geisha lots, expect a bright, refined cup with florals, citrus brightness, and silky texture.

products.title: Ethiopia Sidama Bensa Qonqona Lychee Double Anaerobic Honey
products.body_html:
Region: Sidama, Bensa, Ethiopia
Producer: Qonqona Washing Station (operated by Daye Bensa)
Varietal: 74110 / 74112 Heirloom
Process: Lychee Double Anaerobic Honey (with lychee yeast fermentation)
Altitude: 1,910 – 2,010 masl
Grade: G1
Taste Note: Lychee, white peach, sweet floral, fruit tea finish
Brewing method: Filter or Espresso

Roaster Note

This cup opens with an unmistakable burst of lychee sweetness, clear and elegant, that sets the tone from the first sip. As it cools, juicy notes of white peach and hints of tropical fruit emerge, layered with delicate florals. The dual anaerobic honey process lends a syrupy body yet keeps the cup remarkably clean, finishing with a refreshing fruit-tea character. There’s a playful brightness balanced by soft sweetness, making it both complex and easy to enjoy. It feels like a carefully orchestrated flavor journey — vibrant, layered, and memorable.

 

Bean Info

This coffee comes from the Qonqona Washing Station in Bensa, Sidama, managed by Daye Bensa — a company widely recognized for its quality and farmer-support initiatives. The lot uses Ethiopia’s renowned heirloom varieties 74110 and 74112, cultivated at altitudes of 1,910–2,010 meters, where cool mountain conditions allow cherries to ripen slowly, concentrating sugars and aromatics.

The “Lychee Double Anaerobic Honey” process is what makes this lot special. Fresh cherries undergo an initial sealed anaerobic fermentation, then are re-fermented with carefully selected lychee yeast before being honey-dried. This dual fermentation produces clean, focused, and natural lychee and peach aromatics, while the honey process layers in sweetness and depth.

Daye Bensa is known for supporting surrounding smallholder farmers with agronomy training and better incomes. The Qonqona station is considered a model facility in Sidama, where precise processing and farmer care result in consistently outstanding coffees.

products.title: Costa Rica Canet Musician Mozart
products.body_html:
Region: Tarrazú, Costa Rica
Producer: Canet Estate
Varietal: Caturra / Catuai
Process: Raisin Honey
Altitude: 1,600 – 1,900 masl
Taste Note: Muscat grape, kiwi, strawberry, complex florals, lingering fruit sweetness
Brewing method: Filter or Espresso

Roaster Note
This Mozart lot is a symphony of fruits and florals that lingers long after each sip. It opens with a vivid muscat grape sweetness that lasts beautifully on the palate, evolving into a medley of bright fruits reminiscent of kiwi and fresh strawberries. Layers of complex florals weave throughout, giving the cup a lifted elegance. The raisin honey process enriches the texture, adding both depth and clarity to the fruit expression. Each sip feels dynamic yet harmonious — a coffee that balances vibrancy with refinement. Its long, fruit-driven finish makes it a truly memorable and contemplative experience.

Bean Info

The Canet Estate is nestled in Costa Rica’s renowned Tarrazú region, one of the world’s most celebrated coffee origins for high-altitude cultivation. Known for its “Musician Series,” Canet names each lot after a classical composer, with each representing a unique processing innovation. The “Mozart” lot employs a raisin honey process: ripe cherries are partially sun-dried into a raisin-like state, then pulped while retaining mucilage before completing fermentation and drying. This hybrid method preserves fruit depth while amplifying sweetness, producing a layered, winey profile.

Grown at altitudes of 1,600–1,900 meters, the cooler nights and volcanic soil help develop slow cherry maturation, concentrating sugars and aromatic complexity. The result is a cup that bridges bright fruit notes with refined florals, showing the experimental yet meticulous craftsmanship of the Canet producers.

products.title: Peru Los Santos Geisha (Washed)
products.body_html:
Region: Cusco, Peru
Producer: Los Santos smallholder farmers
Varietal: Geisha
Process: Washed
Altitude: 1,700 – 1,900 masl
Taste Note: Floral, citrus blossom, bergamot, honey sweetness, tea-like body

Roaster Note

This Geisha greets you with an airy bouquet of jasmine and citrus blossom, unfolding with refined elegance. Beneath the florals, a subtle umami note adds depth and intrigue, giving the cup a savory counterpoint to its delicate aromatics. The body is silky and tea-like, evoking the sensation of sipping fine high-mountain tea. The washed process allows remarkable clarity, balancing gentle honey sweetness with a clean, lingering finish. Each sip feels graceful and meditative — a coffee to slow down with, where refinement and purity take center stage.


Bean info

Finca Los Santos is a family-run farm in the Amazonas region of northern Peru, managed today by third-generation farmer José Santos Requejo. Established in 1941, the farm sits between 1,700–1,900 meters above sea level, where cool mountain air, frequent cloud cover, and rich volcanic soil provide ideal conditions for cultivating Geisha. Around 10% of the farm is dedicated to Geisha, with cherries carefully hand-picked, washed, and dried on raised beds under solar driers for even consistency.

Los Santos participates in Peru’s agrarian research initiatives (PNIA) to improve coffee quality and sustainability, using organic pest management and intercropping with bananas, yuca, and corn to support biodiversity. Their dedication has been recognized internationally — including a Cup of Excellence Top 10 placement in 2023. This washed Geisha reflects both terroir and farmer care: clean, floral, and refined.

products.title: Nutty Caramel Blend
products.body_html: This is a classic blend of Brazilian and Colombian beans. We've chosen Brazilian beans for their sweetness, apple-like character, and nutty notes, and roasted them to a medium-dark profile. Combine that with the full-bodied, almost dark chocolate-like and caramel notes of Colombian and Guatemala beans. You can taste baked nuts, cocoa, and sweet caramelized flavors when you drink it black. When paired with milk, it's like drinking a creamy, cocoa-based beverage with caramelized milk flavors. Great as a daily comfort drink.

products.title: Dark Chocolate Blend
products.body_html:
This blend brings together coffees from Guatemala, Colombia, Honduras, and Indonesia, roasted to a medium-dark profile for depth and strength. In the cup, you’ll find rich dark chocolate, toffee sweetness, and a touch of pecan nuttiness. The roast emphasizes a bold body, low acidity, and long-lasting bittersweet cocoa finish that makes it a reliable daily brew.

Perfect on its own as a strong, satisfying cup, and equally excellent as the base for flavoured coffee drinks, mochas, or lattes, where its chocolatey backbone shines through.

products.title: Panama Janson Geisha Lot 359
products.body_html:
Origin: Volcán, Panama
Producer: Janson Family Farms
Variety: Green Tip Geisha
Process: Washed
Altitude: 1,800 m
Tasting Notes: Green apple, sencha tea, cantaloupe, floral, sweet finish


Roaster’s Note:

A pristine example of Panama’s famed washed Geisha. Bright green apple and fresh sencha lead the cup, opening into sweet cantaloupe and delicate florals. Silky, clean, and endlessly refined — a coffee to slow down and savor.


Bean Info
From the highlands of Volcán, Panama, this exceptional Green Tip Geisha is grown at 1,800 m by the renowned Janson Family Farms. Carefully washed processed to highlight its clarity and elegance, this lot offers a refined cup that is both vibrant and delicate.

Expect a silky mouthfeel and a harmonious flavor profile of green apple, sencha tea, and cantaloupe, underscored by subtle floral notes and a clean, lingering sweetness. A truly remarkable coffee that showcases why Janson Geishas are among the world’s most celebrated.

products.title: Panama Mama Cata Irma Geisha (Washed)
products.body_html:
Region: Boquete
Altitude: 1500-1700m
Processing: Washed
Taste Note: Jasmine, honeydew melon, grapefruit, white grape, and Jin Xuan oolong tea
Brewing Method: Filter
Goes well with milk? Yes - if you like lightly floralish with caramel milk based coffee

Roaster Note:
This Geisha from the renowned Mama Cata Estate in Panama is a showcase of elegance and clarity. The washed process highlights the variety’s signature jasmine-like florals, layered with bergamot, sweet citrus, and stone fruit brightness. As it cools, the cup unfolds with tea-like delicacy and a lingering honey sweetness.

I gave it a light roast to preserve its clarity and high-toned aromatics, resulting in a cup that’s refined, complex, and endlessly refreshing. A true connoisseur’s coffee—delicate yet expressive, and one that rewards slow sipping.

 

Bean Info
Mama Cata Estate: Established in 1959 and managed by the Garrido family, it's located at 1,500-1,700 meters above sea level and known for quality improvements implemented by current owner Jose David Garrido Perez.

Irma Estate: A newer Garrido family estate in El Salto, Boquete (1,350-1,400m), specializing in high-quality coffee through meticulous processing.

products.title: Colombia Inza Wuchii Decaf
products.body_html:
Region: Inzá, Cauca, Colombia
Producer: Smallholder farmers, Wuchii area
Varietal: Mixed (Caturra, Colombia, Castillo)
Process: EA Sugarcane Decaf (Natural Ethyl Acetate method)
Altitude: 1,600–2,000 masl
Taste Note: Red fruit, caramel sweetness, hint of cocoa
Brewing method: Filter / Espresso
Goes well with milk?: Yes – smooth caramel chocolate cup

Roaster Notes
I roasted this decaf to highlight its gentle fruit sweetness and smooth body, making it an easy and comforting cup any time of day. In the cup you’ll find soft red fruit notes, caramel sweetness, and a hint of cocoa. Balanced and versatile, it drinks well black for its clarity, and with milk it develops into a creamy caramel chocolate cup.

A true daily drinker—without the caffeine.


Bean info

This decaf lot comes from the Inzá region of Cauca, Colombia, an area known for its high-altitude farms and smallholder producers. The coffee is processed using the Ethyl Acetate (EA) Sugarcane method, a natural decaffeination technique developed in Colombia. Locally sourced sugarcane is fermented to produce ethyl acetate, which gently removes caffeine while preserving the coffee’s natural sweetness and vibrant character.

The result is a decaf that doesn’t compromise on flavor—showcasing the terroir of Inzá with clarity and depth.

products.title: Malaysia Sabah Ranau
products.body_html:
Region: Sabah Ranau
Producer: Sabarica
Process: Anaerobic Natural
Varietals: Catimor
Altitude: 1500M
Flavor Notes: Guava, Pineapple, Passionfruits, Mulberry, hints of wine
Brewing Method: Espresso and Filter
Goes well with milk?: Yes

Roaster Notes
I roasted this lot to highlight its tropical fruit brightness and wine-like complexity from the anaerobic process, while keeping a rounded, drinkable body. In the cup, you’ll find juicy tropical fruit, sweet fermented notes, and a bold, full-bodied character. With milk, the sweetness softens into a fruit-laced cocoa cup—distinctive, memorable, and a proud showcase of Sabah coffee’s potential.


Bean info

This lot comes from Sabarica Coffee, a pioneering specialty coffee producer based in Ranau, Sabah, Malaysia. Working closely with local smallholder farmers at the foothills of Mount Kinabalu, Sabarica has been at the forefront of elevating Sabah-grown coffee to the specialty stage.

The varietal here is Catimor, cultivated at highland altitudes in Ranau where cool nights and fertile volcanic soil create favorable conditions. What makes this coffee stand out is its anaerobic fermentation process—the cherries are fermented in sealed tanks without oxygen, allowing fruity, wine-like flavors to develop before being carefully dried.

The result is a distinctly Sabah cup profile: bold and full-bodied with lively tropical fruit notes, a sweet fermented edge, and a complexity that showcases both the potential of Catimor and the innovation of local processing methods. This coffee also reflects the growing movement of Sabah coffee producers who are experimenting with advanced post-harvest techniques to put Malaysia on the global specialty coffee map.

products.title: Costa Rica Hacienda Sonora
products.body_html:
Region: Central Valley 
Mill: Hacienda Sonora
Process: Black Honey
Varietals: Caturra
Altitude: 1500M
Flavor Notes: Dark cocoa, Floral, Red Wine, Almond, Cherry
Brewing Method: Espresso and Filter
Goes well with milk?: Yes

Roaster Notes
This black honey lot from Hacienda Sonora offers a smooth mix of almond chocolate and raisin sweetness, layered with subtle wine-like complexity that lingers in the aftertaste. Full-bodied with low acidity, it’s easy to enjoy as a black cup. With milk, the coating cocoa deepens and the winey character adds strength and depth to the brew.


Bean info
Hacienda Sonora is nestled in Costa Rica’s Central Valley and is well known for its unwavering commitment to sustainability. Managed by father-and-son duo Alberto and Diego Guardia, the estate has been dedicated to producing high-quality coffee since the 1970s.

The farm is powered entirely by hydroelectric energy, relying fully on renewable sources. It also uses professionally treated water for irrigation. More than a quarter of the land is preserved as natural forest, underscoring Sonora’s strong environmental values.

Hacienda Sonora cultivates a diverse range of Arabica varieties, with Caturra being a key cultivar. A natural mutation of Bourbon, Caturra is compact and high-yielding. Thanks to its Bourbon lineage, it offers rich flavors with floral and fruity notes.

The estate is known for its expertise in honey and natural processing, methods that not only conserve water but also enhance the coffee’s sweetness and complexity. Sonora’s signature black honey process, often combined with natural drying, creates a cup with deeper flavor expressions, including chocolate and fruity undertones.

These thoughtful farming and processing practices have made Hacienda Sonora a leader in Costa Rica’s specialty coffee scene, earning widespread recognition from international buyers and coffee enthusiasts around the world.

products.title: Brazil Espinho Microlot, Paraiso
products.body_html:
Farm/Producer: Espinho / Luiz Eduardo Vilela

Varietal: Paraiso

Process: Natural

Altitude: 950 - 1,150 masl

Roaster Note
This microlot from Fazenda Espinho, Brazil breaks away from the classic nut-and-chocolate profile you’d expect from Brazilian coffees. Instead, it reveals a more fruit-forward side—ripe grape notes with a lively apple-like acidity, gently balanced by a touch of nuttiness.

I gave it a medium roast to preserve the clarity of those fruit tones while keeping it round and approachable. The result is a cup that’s bright but not overly fruity, with a smooth body that makes it enjoyable both as a clean filter brew or a nuanced espresso.


Bean Info:

Paraiso varietal from Brazil. Paraiso was developed by EPAMIG (Minas Gerais Agricultural Research and Development Company) and released in 2012. It is a hybrid of Yellow Catuai and Timor. Paraiso is prized for its high productivity and strong disease resistance, as well as its high cup quality.

This natural lot was machine harvested and then separated by density and ripeness with ripe cherries being selected. From here the coffee was taken to dry on the patios and turned regularly until it reached 11.35% moisture. Then the coffee was rested in wooden silos for 10 days before being milled and bagged and taken to the cooperative.

This coffee tastes nothing like your typical Brazilian coffee. It’s vibrant ripe fruit notes shone brightest on the cupping table. This is the best score of Brazilian coffee we got!

products.title: Brazil Sao Benedito Microlot
products.body_html:
Farm/Producer: Sao Benedito / Eduardo Costa

Location: Ilicinea, South of Minas

Varietal: Yellow Bourbon

Process: Natural

Altitude: 1,200 MASL

Cup Profile: Macadamia, brown sugar, stewed apple


Roaster Note:

A creamy, buttery note that provides a smooth mouthfeel, caramel-like sweetness and gentle, fruity acidity reminiscent of slow-cooked orchard fruits.

This coffee delivers a balanced and approachable profile, making it suitable for both filter and espresso preparations. Its harmonious blend of nutty, sweet, and fruity notes makes it an excellent choice for those seeking a versatile and comforting brew


Bean Info:

Eduardo represents the third generation of coffee growers in his family, continuing a tradition that began with his grandparents in the microregion of Areias, Ilicínea. Despite his parents taking different paths, he remained dedicated to coffee, actively managing the farm alongside his grandparents. After his grandmother's passing, he took over part of the estate and expanded with new plantations, focusing on innovation and excellence. With a background in agricultural technology and philosophy, Eduardo blends tradition with modern practices, prioritizing sustainability and quality while honouring his family's legacy.

products.title: Guatemala Antigua SHB
products.body_html:
Varietal: Caturra
Process: Washed
Altitude:1500 M
Grade: SHB
Taste note:
Black: Mild citrusy, Sweet, Medium-bodied, Cocoa, Balanced
Latte: Orange Creamiscle, Caramel, Almonds, Mellow and Creamy

Roaster Note
In the cup, expect sweet citrus, red apple, and milk chocolate, balanced with a smooth sweetness and medium body. It’s versatile—refreshing as a filter brew, yet round and balanced for espresso. With milk, it develops into a gentle caramel cup, with layering chocolate and even hints of floral.

Bean Info
From the renowned coffee region of Antigua, Guatemala, this lot comes from high-altitude farms (above 1,500 masl) where rich volcanic soil and cool nights help create Antigua’s signature profile. The Caturra varietal, fully washed and strictly hard bean (SHB) grade, delivers a clean, structured cup.

products.title: Ethiopia Lucy Geisha (Washed)
products.body_html:
Region. Bench Maji
Processing station. Lucy Station
Altitude. 2280 masl
Varietal. Geisha
Processing. Washed
Taste Profile. Elderflower, Jasmine, Coffee Blossom, Apple, Passionfruit, Lemon

Roaster Note
You’ll get lots of white and yellow florals here—think elderflower and ginger blossom—balanced with sweet caramel and a touch of candied lemon. As a black coffee it’s bright and citrusy, almost like sipping lemonade. Add milk and it softens into a caramel-floral milk tea vibe that’s light, smooth, and super easy to enjoy

Bean info
This coffee comes from Lucy Geisha, located in the Geisha region of Bench Maji, Ethiopia — the very birthplace of Geisha coffee. Often referred to as the "mother of Geisha," this region is where all Geisha varieties trace their roots, whether Panamanian, Guatemalan, or Taiwanese.

Named after the famous hominid fossil believed to be the origin of humankind, the Lucy processing station was founded with a similar mission: to share the purest, most flavorful Geisha coffee with the world. Though officially established less than a decade ago, Lucy has quickly risen to prominence, producing coffees that rival even the finest Central and South American Geishas.

This success is thanks to the region's ideal terroir — rich soil, balanced temperature shifts, and perfect rainfall — which consistently yield cherries bursting with complex, captivating flavor.

products.title: Costa Rica San Ramon Hummingbird
products.body_html:
Region: Tarrazú
Mill: San Roman Mill
Process: Natural (Sun-dried)
Varietals: Caturra, Catuai
Altitude: 1700M
Flavor Notes: Grape, apple, blueberry jam, black tea
Brewing Method: Espresso and Filter
Goes well with milk?: Yes

Roaster Notes
This coffee leans into ripe tropical fruit notes, with an intriguing “durian-like” richness when paired with milk that gradually softens into pleasant cocoa. As a black cup, it shows layered complexity—sometimes bold with jackfruit-like ripeness, other times cleaner with bright fruit tones. Overall, it’s a strong-bodied, full-flavoured coffee with medium-low acidity, offering a unique and memorable experience.


Bean info
The Tarrazú region is located in the southwest of Costa Rica, near Volcán Poás, and faces the Pacific Ocean. It benefits from a unique microclimate, including fertile volcanic soil, ideal temperatures, sunlight, and humidity — all of which contribute to producing perfectly ripe red coffee cherries.

Throughout the production process, manual weeding and eco-friendly farming practices are used, strictly avoiding chemical fertilizers and pesticides. This natural approach results in coffees that truly represent the characteristics of the region: sweet and fragrant aroma, rich body, medium acidity, and a clean finish with notes of stone fruit, spices, and pleasant sweetness.

Only fully ripe red cherries are selectively handpicked, with strict quality control throughout the processing. The cherries are washed, fermented, and sun-dried at the mill. The parchment coffee is then moved to raised beds for further sun drying, ensuring even moisture content before hulling and export.

This is a modern dry-washed process, where 0–10% of the mucilage and fruit is intentionally left on the beans. Through gentle fermentation and a slow 25-day natural drying period, the method highlights the precision and terroir of Costa Rica’s micro-mills. The result is a coffee with excellent clarity and complexity, perfectly balanced through careful and measured fermentation.

Roaster Note
This coffee’s strength is its creamy nutty flavor, smooth and comforting from the first sip. We’ve taken the roast slightly deeper to bring out a soft cocoa note, giving it that nutty–cocoa profile most people love. Its gentle orange note adds a touch of brightness that turns into a caramel-like sweetness, especially when paired with milk. Easy to enjoy every day, it’s a cup that feels both familiar and satisfying.

Bean Info
La Abejilla ("The Little Bee") coffee comes from the San Vito region in southern Costa Rica, near the border with Panama. Surrounded by the Coto Brus mountain range, the area enjoys a large diurnal temperature range and abundant rainfall, with distinct wet and dry seasons. These climate conditions are ideal for healthy coffee tree growth and the development of high-quality coffee beans.

La Abejilla coffee is the result of collaboration among many smallholder farmers in the region. Local cooperatives provide these farmers with technical support and marketing channels, helping them secure fair prices and stable income in the international market. The farmers use sustainable and organic farming practices, avoiding chemical pesticides and fertilizers to protect both the environment and soil health.

These efforts result in a coffee with bright acidity, vibrant fruitiness, and a sweet, well-rounded flavor profile.
